blockers.problem: [P1] Worker keys grant unrestricted access to the brain owner's account.
blockers.exploit_or_failure: ensureWorkerKey appends the worker public key to the brain's authorized_keys without a forced command or restrictions. A worker can use its own key to execute arbitrary commands as the brain owner, read that account's GitHub credentials and SSH private keys, or modify the queue and approval state. ForwardAgent=no on normal client calls does not restrict what the key can authorize.
blockers.fix: Use a dedicated restricted worker identity with a forced-command dispatcher permitting only authenticated queue operations and read-only access to approved mirrors. Deny arbitrary shells, forwarding and credential paths; bind queue identity to the authenticated key. Test rejected shell and credential-read requests.

blockers.problem: [P1] Every queue transport call passes an extra ssh executable as the first argument.
blockers.exploit_or_failure: sshArgs returns ['ssh', '-T', ...], but next, claim, renew and report pass that entire array to run('ssh', ...). The resulting command starts with ssh ssh -T ..., making ssh the destination instead of the configured brain. Normal workers cannot pull or maintain tickets. An inert transport capture reproduced the extra argument; the harness uses an in-memory transport and never exercises this path.
blockers.fix: Return arguments only or pass sshArgs(...).slice(1) consistently. Add a transport test asserting executable, destination, options and remote command for all four operations.

blockers.problem: [P1] JSON stringification does not safely quote SSH remote-command arguments.
blockers.exploit_or_failure: The remote shell evaluates dollar substitutions and backticks inside JSON's double quotes. Job IDs are only required to be nonempty strings, so a queued ID containing $(...) becomes executable shell content in claim, renew and report. An inert reproduction changed the literal ID batch:$(printf INJECTED) into batch:INJECTED when the generated arguments were interpreted by /bin/sh. Once the transport argv bug is fixed, this executes on the brain as its owner.
blockers.fix: Use a fixed remote dispatcher with structured input over stdin, or correctly quote every argument for the remote shell and validate identifiers. Test dollar substitutions, backticks, quotes and newlines as literal data.

blockers.problem: [P1] The default subprocess helper does not implement its callers' result or stdin contract.
blockers.exploit_or_failure: Promisified execFile resolves successful commands with stdout/stderr but no code, and ignores the input option. syncRunner and runBrainMove therefore reject successful rsync results because undefined !== 0; a move leaves the source queue paused. Worker and watchdog service installers pass scripts to bash -s through input, so no script is delivered. Both behaviors were reproduced with harmless local Node subprocesses. Harness stubs always return code:0 and conceal the failures.
blockers.fix: Provide one subprocess adapter that writes and closes stdin, returns a numeric exit code on success and has a consistent failure contract. Use it for bootstrap, service installation, rsync and handoff. Test the real adapter, including a successful move and recovery after transfer failure.

blockers.problem: [P1] Installed macOS services use a literal tilde runner path.
blockers.exploit_or_failure: The worker and brainwatch plists put ~/.project-swarm/current/tools/swarm.mjs in ProgramArguments. launchd invokes Node directly, so no shell expands the tilde; Node tries to load a nonexistent path under the working directory and exits. The executable path is also copied from the installing machine's process.execPath, which may not exist on the target. This remains broken after fixing script delivery.
blockers.fix: Resolve the target user's home and Node executable on the target, write absolute ProgramArguments, and supply the PATH required by installed lane CLIs. Verify an actual installed service reaches the worker loop.

blockers.problem: [P1] Brain promotion never fences the old brain and resumes both queue copies.
blockers.exploit_or_failure: runBrainMove starts Watch on the target but never stops or disables the source orchestrator or its queue endpoints, then removes pauses on both machines. The only lock is a local file held for the duration of the move, so independent watchdogs can promote different targets and a partitioned source can continue operating. Two copies of the same queued ticket can be claimed independently. The start command also masks failure with || true, so promotion can succeed without a new process.
blockers.fix: Implement a fenced leadership epoch that queue mutations and orchestrators must validate, serialize promotion across machines, stop or fence the previous writer, and verify target readiness before committing leadership. Do not resume a former brain as a writer. Add partition and concurrent-promotion tests.

blockers.problem: [P1] Handoff copies an incomplete, mutable state snapshot without restoring the target projects.
blockers.exploit_or_failure: Only the local state directory is rsynced. Project snapshots remain archived under state/projects; restoreProjectState is never called, and the project registry, machine registry and repo mirrors are not transferred or reconstructed. Fresh targets cannot discover the old projects or serve their mirrors. Snapshot failures are swallowed. Renew/report writes continue on the source during the copy, so a completion after the copy can be absent on the new brain and later requeued. A watchdog on another machine copies its own local state rather than the failed brain's state. The handoff test disables sync and startup and supplies an empty project list.
blockers.fix: Make handoff a verified state-transfer transaction: persist and replicate authoritative state before failure, reconcile running lease/report updates, transfer the catalogs and mirror access, restore project state to valid target roots, and abort on missing snapshots. Test a populated project and a completion concurrent with handoff.

blockers.problem: [P1] Running workers never reload the brain pointer after handoff.
blockers.exploit_or_failure: brain and transport are captured once before the infinite worker loop. Updating brain.json does not change later reachability probes, pulls, renewals or reports. After a move, workers keep using the old brain indefinitely; if it is alive they mutate its obsolete queue, and if it is down they stop making progress while the target expires copied leases.
blockers.fix: Reload and validate leadership between pulls and provide an explicit fenced transfer protocol for in-flight renewals and reports. Switch the transport and mirror endpoint together. Test a worker that remains running across a brain change.

blockers.problem: [P1] Lease protection starts after preparation and silently ignores lease loss.
blockers.exploit_or_failure: A ticket is claimed before executeItem, but its heartbeat starts only after cloning/fetching and worktree preparation. Cloning permits a one-hour timeout while the lease lasts fifteen minutes, allowing another worker to reclaim the ticket before the first starts its job. During execution every renewal failure is swallowed, so a partitioned worker continues running even after another worker takes the expired lease.
blockers.fix: Start lease maintenance immediately after claim and cover all preparation. Use a lease generation/fencing token, enforce a renewal deadline, and terminate the job process tree before ownership can be lost. Test slow preparation and a renewal failure followed by reassignment.

blockers.problem: [P1] Claim bypasses queue pause and lane eligibility checks.
blockers.exploit_or_failure: Only nextWorkerItem checks the pause file and per-machine cooldown. claimWorkerItem checks only that the item is queued. A worker that fetched an item before handoff can claim it after the pause; a direct claim also takes a cooling lane. An in-memory reproduction showed next returning null for a paused queue while claim successfully leased the same item.
blockers.fix: Recheck pause, authenticated machine eligibility and lane availability inside the claim transaction. Serialize pause establishment with claims, and test both next-then-pause-then-claim and next-then-cooldown-then-claim races.

blockers.problem: [P1] Global queue IDs collide across projects and silently discard work.
blockers.exploit_or_failure: itemId contains only the sanitized manifest basename and job ID, truncated to 120 characters. Two projects with batch.json/build both map to batch.json:build; enqueueManifest treats the second as already queued or done and skips it. This was reproduced with different project names and manifest directories. Truncation creates additional collisions for long IDs.
blockers.fix: Namespace IDs with a stable project identity and full manifest identity, using a collision-resistant digest where necessary. Preserve deliberate idempotency within a batch and test equal basenames/job IDs across projects and long IDs.

blockers.problem: [P1] Reports can complete unleased work or overwrite terminal results without owning a lease.
blockers.exploit_or_failure: Holder validation runs only when status is leased. Once an expired lease is swept to queued, any holder can mark the item done or failed; the same applies to already completed items. An in-memory reproduction requeued a ticket and then completed it using an unrelated holder. Stale reports can thus close reassigned work or overwrite its accepted result.
blockers.fix: Require a current, unexpired lease with matching holder and generation for state transitions. Allow idempotent terminal reports only when they match the previously accepted generation and result. Test stale reports after sweep, requeue and completion.

blockers.problem: [P1] Requeued tickets cannot run again on the same worker worktree path.
blockers.exploit_or_failure: prepareWorktree deterministically uses the item ID for both directory and branch and always runs git worktree add -B. executeItem leaves that worktree behind. After a rate limit, expired lease or failed attempt, a later claim on the same worker hits an existing worktree and throws; runWorkerOnce does not catch preparation failures or hand the lease back. The intended cooldown-and-retry path repeatedly crashes instead of executing.
blockers.fix: Allocate worktrees per lease attempt or safely resume a verified matching worktree, retaining prior outputs. Catch preparation failures and report or requeue them explicitly. Test two executions of the same ticket on one worker after a rate-limit requeue.

blockers.problem: [P1] Ghost safety conditions are not monitored while a ticket runs.
blockers.exploit_or_failure: runWorkerOnce evaluates charger, lid and reachability once, then awaits executeItem, which can run for four hours. No code re-probes during execution or uses DEFAULT_GRACE_MS. A ghost unplugged or taken away immediately after claim continues work and renewals without the documented grace-period handback; if it sleeps, the ticket can be reassigned while its old process later resumes.
blockers.fix: Monitor ghost conditions throughout preparation and execution, stop accepting work immediately when unsafe, and cancel/checkpoint the process tree and return the fenced lease after the grace period. Test charger removal, lid closure and loss of brain connectivity during a running ticket.

blockers.problem: [P1] Mirror cloning ignores the worker SSH key established by machine add.
blockers.exploit_or_failure: ensureRepo accepts key but never passes it to git clone or fetch. machine add creates ~/.ssh/swarm_ed25519, a nondefault identity filename, without configuring a worker-side SSH host entry. On a freshly registered worker with no other authorized identity, queue SSH using -i can succeed while the first clone fails authentication. The exception escapes after claim and leaves the ticket leased until timeout; the executeItem test stubs repository preparation out.
blockers.fix: Provide a safely constructed Git SSH transport using the configured identity, noninteractive authentication and explicit host-key handling for both clone and fetch. Test a fresh worker whose only authorized key is swarm_ed25519.

blockers.problem: [P1] Lane override changes scheduling metadata but not the agent actually executed.
blockers.exploit_or_failure: enqueueManifest stores laneOverride in item.lane but retains the original manifestData unchanged. executeItem writes that manifest and invokes swarm run without an agent override. A Claude job enqueued with --lane codex is eligible for a Codex worker, yet still invokes Claude, including when the machine's Claude lane is cooling or unavailable. Cooldown reporting is then attributed to the wrong lane.
blockers.fix: Resolve and validate the executable lane once, then use that same resolved manifest/job for eligibility, invocation and outcome attribution. Reject incompatible overrides or rewrite the selected job deliberately. Test an override where the original lane is cooling.

summary: Fail: 16 blockers in machine security, transport, service startup, handoff and ticket ownership/retry behavior. The supplied machine harness passes all 17 tests, but its stubs bypass the production SSH/process paths and its brain-move test disables transfer and startup. Reviewed only the supplied diff and context; no live SSH, service installation, model calls or deployment were performed. Inert reproductions confirmed the transport argv/quoting defects, subprocess contract mismatch, cross-project queue collision, pause bypass and unowned report acceptance.

checksRun.name: Diff-extracted inert transport and in-memory queue defect reproductions
Diff-extracted defaultRun exit-code and stdin contract reproductions
Live multi-machine handoff, SSH and service startup
